questions.text: Per Sec. 809-b, if a vent shaft does not open directly to outer air at the top, what is the minimum free area requirement for the skylight or fixed louver covering?

options.text: Equal to the minimum required shaft area (1.00 sq.m.), ensuring adequate ventilation and compliance with natural light requirements.
At least 50% of the shaft cross-sectional area, which is necessary to maintain airflow and prevent moisture accumulation.
Not less than the maximum required cross-sectional area of the shaft
Twice the actual cross-sectional area of the shaft to ensure redundancy in ventilation and light penetration.

questions.rationale: Section 809-b requires that the net free area of the skylight or louver opening equal or exceed the maximum required cross-sectional area of the shaft — not a reduced or minimum value. The code says 'maximum required' specifically to prevent designers from covering a large shaft with a small louvered panel. A shaft requiring 1.50 sq.m. must have covering with at least 1.50 sq.m. of free area.

questions.text: At what specific shaft height does the Sec. 809-a formula (0.10 sq.m. per meter) exactly equal the absolute minimum area requirement of 1.00 sq.m.?

options.text: 5 meters
6 meters
10 meters
12 meters

questions.rationale: At exactly 10.00 m height: 0.10 sq.m. × 10.00 m = 1.00 sq.m. — the formula result equals the absolute minimum. Below 10.00 m, the absolute minimum of 1.00 sq.m. governs (the formula would yield less). Above 10.00 m, the formula result governs. This 10-meter threshold is a key reference point for board exam calculations.

questions.text: According to PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 708, what is the maximum PSO for Group A Dwellings on a corner lot versus an inside lot?

options.text: Corner lot: 80%; Inside lot: 90%
Corner lot: 85%; Inside lot: 80%
Corner lot: 90%; Inside lot: 80%
Corner lot: 75%; Inside lot: 70%

questions.rationale: The inside lot (80%) and corner lot (90%) PSO limits for Group A are the reverse of what many candidates assume. The confusion arises because in other occupancy groups, corner lots typically have HIGHER PSO allowances (e.g., R-1 corner = 55% vs. R-1 inside = 50%). But for Group A dwellings specifically, Section 708 overrides the general table with these higher residential coverage allowances.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII Section 708, what are the minimum dimensional requirements for a stairway serving a Group A dwelling?

options.text: 750 mm minimum clear width, with maximum 200 mm riser height and minimum 200 mm tread run
900 mm minimum clear width, with maximum 180 mm riser height and minimum 250 mm tread run
600 mm minimum clear width, with maximum 250 mm riser height and minimum 250 mm tread run
1,000 mm minimum clear width, with maximum 150 mm riser height and minimum 300 mm tread run

questions.rationale: Section 708 requires stairs serving Group A dwellings to have at least 750 mm clear width, with risers not exceeding 200 mm and treads of not less than 200 mm run. The dimensions support safe, comfortable ascent and descent for a single residential occupancy.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 808, what is the minimum window opening area required for a habitable room in a Group A dwelling?

options.text: At least 10 percent of the floor area of the room, with a minimum opening of 1.00 sq.m
At least 15 percent of the floor area of the room, with a minimum opening of 1.20 sq.m
At least 12.5 percent of the floor area of the room, with a minimum opening of 1.50 sq.m
At least 5 percent of the floor area of the room, with a minimum opening of 0.60 sq.m

questions.rationale: Section 808 requires window openings in habitable rooms of Group A dwellings to be at least 10 percent of the floor area of the room, and in no case less than 1.00 sq.m. The window must open directly to a court, yard, public space, or air shaft.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 805, what is the minimum ceiling height for a habitable room in a Group A dwelling, and what reduced ceiling height is allowed for rooms that are not naturally ventilated?

options.text: 2.70 m for naturally ventilated rooms; 2.40 m for rooms that are not naturally ventilated
3.00 m for naturally ventilated rooms; 2.70 m for rooms that are not naturally ventilated
2.40 m for naturally ventilated rooms; 2.10 m for rooms that are not naturally ventilated
2.50 m for naturally ventilated rooms; 2.20 m for rooms that are not naturally ventilated

questions.rationale: Section 805 sets the minimum ceiling height at 2.70 m for naturally ventilated habitable rooms in Group A dwellings; where the room is not naturally ventilated, a 2.40 m minimum ceiling height applies.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII Section 708, what minimum setback from the side and rear property lines must a Group A dwelling observe, in addition to the percent-of-site-occupancy and the Civil Code easements of light and view?

options.text: At least 2.00 m from every property line
At least 1.00 m from every property line
At least 3.00 m from every property line
At least 1.50 m from every property line

questions.rationale: Section 708 requires a Group A dwelling to be set back at least 2.00 m from every property line. This minimum does not override the larger Civil Code easements of light and view, which apply on top of any code setback.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 807, what are the minimum floor area requirements for a kitchen and for a combined toilet and bath in a Group A dwelling?

options.text: Kitchen: at least 3.00 sq.m with 1.50 m minimum dimension; toilet and bath: at least 1.20 sq.m with 0.90 m minimum dimension
Kitchen: at least 4.50 sq.m with 1.80 m minimum dimension; toilet and bath: at least 1.50 sq.m with 1.00 m minimum dimension
Kitchen: at least 6.00 sq.m with 2.00 m minimum dimension; toilet and bath: at least 2.00 sq.m with 1.20 m minimum dimension
Kitchen: at least 2.40 sq.m with 1.20 m minimum dimension; toilet and bath: at least 1.00 sq.m with 0.75 m minimum dimension

questions.rationale: Section 807 sets minimum floor areas for service spaces smaller than habitable rooms: kitchen at 3.00 sq.m with 1.50 m minimum horizontal dimension, and combined toilet and bath at 1.20 sq.m with 0.90 m minimum horizontal dimension.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 807, what is the minimum floor area and minimum horizontal dimension required for a habitable room in a Group A dwelling?

options.text: 6.00 sq.m floor area with a 2.00 m minimum horizontal dimension
9.00 sq.m floor area with a 2.40 m minimum horizontal dimension
4.50 sq.m floor area with a 1.80 m minimum horizontal dimension
7.50 sq.m floor area with a 2.10 m minimum horizontal dimension

questions.rationale: Section 807 requires habitable rooms in Group A dwellings to have at least 6.00 sq.m of floor area and a minimum horizontal dimension of 2.00 m. Smaller service spaces (kitchen, bath/toilet) are governed by separate minimum areas.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 807, what is the minimum air space required per occupant of a habitable room in a Group A dwelling?

options.text: 10.00 cubic meters of air space per occupant
12.00 cubic meters of air space per occupant
14.00 cubic meters of air space per occupant
9.00 cubic meters of air space per occupant

questions.rationale: Section 807 requires at least 14.00 cubic meters of air space per occupant in habitable rooms of Group A dwellings. Combined with the minimum ceiling height from Section 805, this sets a floor-area-per-person baseline for the room.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 806, why must a habitable room in a Group A dwelling satisfy BOTH the minimum floor area (6.00 sq.m) AND the minimum least horizontal dimension (2.00 m), rather than just one of the two?

options.text: Because both conditions are independent mandatory minima; satisfying one does not excuse the other, and a long narrow room (e.g., 6.00 sq.m at 1.20 m least dimension) is still non-compliant
Because the floor area rule applies only to ground-floor rooms and the least-dimension rule applies only to upper-floor rooms
Because the floor area rule is mandatory but the least-dimension rule is a recommended design guideline that may be waived by the Building Official
Because the two values come from different referral codes and the Code requires the average of the two to be met

questions.rationale: Section 806 imposes both minima simultaneously: 6.00 sq.m of floor area AND 2.00 m least horizontal dimension. A room that meets area but not the least dimension (for example 5.00 m x 1.20 m = 6.00 sq.m but only 1.20 m least dimension) is non-compliant because it would form a functionally unusable 'corridor room'.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Section 806, what is the minimum least dimension for a habitable room, and why is this requirement as important as the floor area minimum?

options.text: 1.50 m; important because it ensures adequate walking space and allows for basic furniture arrangement
2.00 m; important because it prevents long, narrow 'corridor rooms' that technically meet area minimums but are functionally useless for habitation
2.50 m; important because it ensures furniture placement is possible and provides flexibility in room layout
1.20 m; important because it matches the minimum doorway width, ensuring easy access and egress

questions.rationale: The 2.00 m least dimension for habitable rooms equals the minimum corridor width for wheelchair access (Rule VIII accessible design principles) and the minimum court horizontal dimension (Sec. 804). The convergence of the 2.00 m figure across multiple sections helps with recall.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 808, the required window opening of a habitable room in a Group A dwelling must open directly onto which of the following in order to be counted toward the minimum ventilation area?

options.text: A court, yard, public space, or air shaft that has direct access to outer air
A covered carport or garage, provided the opening is at least 1.00 sq.m
An adjacent enclosed room that has its own window, regardless of where that window opens
A roofed-over balcony or lanai of any size, regardless of whether it connects to outer air

questions.rationale: Section 808 requires the required window opening to face directly onto a court, yard, public space, or air shaft with direct access to outer air. A window facing a covered or enclosed space (carport, adjacent enclosed room, roofed lanai without outer-air connection) cannot be counted toward the Section 808 minimum.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII Section 708, what minimum foundation wall thickness and minimum depth below natural ground line are required for a Group A dwelling?

options.text: 250 mm minimum wall thickness; at least 600 mm below the natural ground line
200 mm minimum wall thickness; at least 900 mm below the natural ground line
300 mm minimum wall thickness; at least 750 mm below the natural ground line
100 mm minimum wall thickness; at least 450 mm below the natural ground line

questions.rationale: Section 708 requires foundation walls for Group A dwellings to be at least 250 mm thick and to extend at least 600 mm below the natural ground line, with footings sized to safely transfer all loads to the soil.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 708, what is the maximum lot occupancy (Percent of Site Occupancy) for a Group A dwelling on a corner lot versus an inside lot?

options.text: Corner lot: 90%; inside lot: 80%
Corner lot: 80%; inside lot: 70%
Corner lot: 70%; inside lot: 60%
Corner lot: 100%; inside lot: 90%

questions.rationale: Section 708 limits a Group A dwelling to a maximum of 90 percent of a corner lot and 80 percent of an inside lot. The dwelling must also be at least 2.00 m from the property line and is subject to Civil Code easements of light and view.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII Section 708, when a Group A dwelling uses wooden posts for support, what is the minimum required cross-sectional area of each wooden post?

options.text: 0.025 square meter (e.g., 100 mm x 250 mm) per post
0.040 square meter (e.g., 200 mm x 200 mm) per post
0.060 square meter (e.g., 200 mm x 300 mm) per post
0.090 square meter (e.g., 300 mm x 300 mm) per post

questions.rationale: Section 708 requires wooden posts supporting a Group A dwelling to have a minimum cross-sectional area of 0.025 square meter per post. This is commonly achieved with a 100 mm x 250 mm or equivalent section that aggregates to at least 0.025 sq.m.

questions.text: Under PD 1096, Rule VII, Sec. 708(a), a Group A dwelling must be at least 2 meters from the property line. An architect proposes a corner lot development of 8 m x 12 m (96 sq.m.) with maximum lot coverage. What is the actual achievable building footprint considering BOTH the 90% coverage limit and the 2-meter setback requirement?

options.text: 86 sq.m. — 90% of 96 sq.m., applying only the lot coverage percentage
32 sq.m. — (8−4) x (12−4) = 4 m x 8 m = 32 sq.m. after applying 2 m setback on all sides
48 sq.m. — applying a single 2 m setback on only the two street-facing sides of the corner lot
64 sq.m. — (8−2) x (12−2) = 6 m x 10 m = 60 sq.m., applying the setback on only two sides

questions.rationale: The 2-meter setback applies on all sides per Sec. 708(a). On an 8 m x 12 m lot with 2 m setback on all four sides, the buildable area is (8−4) x (12−4) = 4 m x 8 m = 32 sq.m. The 90% coverage maximum would allow 86 sq.m., but the setback constraint (32 sq.m.) is far more restrictive and governs. This illustrates the critical trap: the coverage percentage and setback minimum are independent constraints, and the more restrictive one governs.

questions.text: Under PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 807, what is the minimum air space per person required for habitable rooms in a Group A dwelling, and how much floor area is needed in a room with a 2.70 m ceiling to legally accommodate 2 persons?

options.text: 10.00 cu.m. per person; a room of 7.40 sq.m. with 2.70 m ceiling provides 20.00 cu.m. for 2 persons
14.00 cu.m. per person; a room needs at least 10.37 sq.m. floor area at 2.70 m ceiling height for 2 persons
14.00 cu.m. per person; a room with 2.70 m ceiling needs 6.00 sq.m. minimum for any number of persons
12.00 cu.m. per person; a room needs at least 8.89 sq.m. floor area at 2.70 m ceiling height for 2 persons

questions.rationale: Sec. 807 requires 14.00 cu.m. of air space per person. For 2 persons: 2 x 14.00 = 28.00 cu.m. needed. With a 2.70 m ceiling: floor area = 28.00 ÷ 2.70 = 10.37 sq.m. minimum. Option A uses the wrong 10 cu.m. value. Option C incorrectly states 6.00 sq.m. is sufficient for any number of persons (6.00 sq.m. is only the minimum area, not an occupancy-independent standard). Option D uses the wrong 12 cu.m. value.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule VII, Sec. 708(a), what are the maximum lot coverage percentages for a Group A single-family dwelling on a corner lot versus an inside lot?

options.text: 80% for corner lots and 70% for inside lots — reflecting the stricter setback requirements on inside lots
90% for corner lots and 80% for inside lots — corner lots have two street frontages allowing more generous coverage
70% for corner lots and 60% for inside lots — the Philippine standard aligning with typical US residential zoning
90% for both lot types — PD 1096 does not distinguish between corner and inside lots for Group A dwellings

questions.rationale: Sec. 708(a) specifies 90% maximum for corner lots and 80% maximum for inside lots. Corner lots have frontage on two streets, giving greater access and light, hence the more generous 90% allowance. Option A reverses the values. Option C is not supported by PD 1096. Option D is incorrect — Sec. 708(a) explicitly distinguishes by lot type.

questions.text: A Group A dwelling is naturally ventilated throughout. Per PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 805, what is the minimum ceiling height for the bedroom on the second floor?

options.text: 2.10 m — the minimum for upper floors in multi-storey buildings under Rule VIII, Sec. 805, applicable only when artificial ventilation is used
2.40 m — the minimum for the second storey under the artificial ventilation provisions, which does not apply to naturally ventilated spaces
2.70 m — the minimum for ALL habitable rooms in naturally ventilated buildings regardless of floor level
1.80 m — the mezzanine clearance which applies to second-floor rooms in compact dwellings, typically used in space-constrained urban areas

questions.rationale: Sec. 805 specifies: for buildings with natural ventilation, all habitable rooms require a minimum ceiling height of 2.70 m regardless of floor level. The descending scale (2.70 m → 2.40 m → 2.10 m) only applies to multi-storey buildings with artificial (mechanical) ventilation. A naturally ventilated second-floor bedroom must still comply with the 2.70 m minimum. Options A and B apply the artificial ventilation scale to a naturally ventilated building. Option D applies the mezzanine clearance.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 806(1)(a), which pair of minimum requirements must BOTH be simultaneously satisfied for a room to qualify as a habitable room in a Group A dwelling?

options.text: Minimum 6.00 sq.m. floor area AND minimum 2.00 m least dimension — both conditions independently required
Minimum 6.00 sq.m. floor area only — the least dimension is a recommended guideline, not a mandatory requirement
Minimum 7.00 sq.m. floor area AND minimum 2.40 m least dimension — the Philippine standard aligned with IRC 2021
Minimum 8.00 sq.m. floor area AND minimum 2.00 m least dimension — applying the larger-room standard for tropical climates

questions.rationale: Sec. 806(1)(a) establishes two simultaneous requirements: 6.00 sq.m. minimum floor area AND 2.00 m minimum least dimension. Both must be met — a room passing area but failing dimension (e.g., 4.0 m x 1.5 m = 6.0 sq.m., least dim 1.5 m < 2.00 m) is non-compliant. Option B incorrectly treats the least dimension as optional. Options C and D cite wrong values.

questions.text: A Group A dwelling has a kitchen that measures 2.00 m x 1.50 m (3.00 sq.m.). Does this kitchen comply with PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 806(1)(b)?

options.text: No — the kitchen fails because the minimum kitchen area is 4.50 sq.m. with a least dimension of 1.80 m
Yes — the kitchen meets the minimum 3.00 sq.m. floor area requirement but must be checked further for the 1.50 m least dimension
Yes — the kitchen satisfies both the 3.00 sq.m. minimum area and the 1.50 m minimum least dimension simultaneously
No — the kitchen fails because 1.50 m is below the 2.00 m least dimension required for all habitable rooms including kitchens

questions.rationale: Sec. 806(1)(b) requires kitchens to have a minimum floor area of 3.00 sq.m. with a minimum least dimension of 1.50 m (not 2.00 m — that is the habitable room standard). A 2.00 m x 1.50 m kitchen = 3.00 sq.m. and has a least dimension of exactly 1.50 m. Both criteria are met exactly. Option A cites wrong values. Option D incorrectly applies the habitable room least dimension (2.00 m) to kitchens.

questions.text: The Building Official inspects a Group A dwelling and finds that the combined toilet and bath room measures 1.05 m x 1.10 m. What is the Code compliance finding under PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 806(1)(c)?

options.text: Compliant — 1.05 m x 1.10 m = 1.155 sq.m., which exceeds the 1.00 sq.m. minimum for bath/toilet rooms
Non-compliant — the area (1.155 sq.m.) exceeds 1.20 sq.m. minimum but the 900 mm least dimension is not met
Non-compliant — the area (1.155 sq.m.) is below the 1.20 sq.m. minimum, and the least dimension (1.05 m) is above 900 mm
Non-compliant — both the area (1.155 sq.m. < 1.20 sq.m.) and the dimension (1.05 m > 900 mm) fail the minimum

questions.rationale: Sec. 806(1)(c) requires bath/toilet rooms to have a minimum area of 1.20 sq.m. AND a minimum least dimension of 900 mm. Area: 1.05 x 1.10 = 1.155 sq.m. — this is BELOW the 1.20 sq.m. minimum, so the room fails on area. Least dimension: 1.05 m = 1050 mm — this exceeds the 900 mm minimum, so it passes on dimension. Non-compliant because area test fails. Option A uses a wrong 1.00 sq.m. threshold. Option D incorrectly states the dimension also fails.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 811, what is the minimum natural ventilation window area required for a habitable room with a floor area of 20 sq.m.?

options.text: 0.80 sq.m. — 4% of 20 sq.m., the IBC standard adopted in the Philippine Code
1.00 sq.m. — the absolute minimum regardless of floor area, applied because 10% of 20 sq.m. equals 2.00 sq.m. but the minimum floor governs
2.00 sq.m. — 10% of the 20 sq.m. floor area per Sec. 811, which exceeds the 1.00 sq.m. absolute minimum
1.60 sq.m. — 8% of 20 sq.m., the IRC standard referenced in the Philippine Code

questions.rationale: Sec. 811 requires natural ventilation window area of at least 10% of the room's floor area, with an absolute minimum of 1.00 sq.m. For a 20 sq.m. room: 10% x 20 = 2.00 sq.m. Since 2.00 sq.m. > 1.00 sq.m. absolute minimum, the percentage rule governs — 2.00 sq.m. is required. Option B incorrectly applies the 1.00 sq.m. floor when the percentage calculation exceeds it. Options A and D apply the IBC and IRC standards respectively, not PD 1096.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule VII, Sec. 708(c), what is the minimum sanitation provision required for EVERY Group A dwelling, regardless of size or number of occupants?

options.text: One sanitary toilet plus adequate washing facilities and adequate drainage facilities — all three elements are mandatory
One sanitary toilet only — washing and drainage facilities are required only for dwellings with more than 4 occupants
Two sanitary toilets plus one laundry area — reflecting the minimum for a standard Philippine family dwelling
One sanitary toilet and one kitchen sink — the kitchen is counted as the washing facility under Sec. 708(c)

questions.rationale: Sec. 708(c) requires every Group A dwelling to have: (1) at least one sanitary toilet, (2) adequate washing facilities, and (3) adequate drainage facilities — all three elements are mandatory with no occupancy-based exception. Option B incorrectly limits washing/drainage to larger households. Option C cites a quantity not in the Code. Option D's interpretation of the kitchen sink as the washing facility is not how Sec. 708(c) is applied.

questions.text: A board exam question states: 'A bedroom in a multi-storey Group A dwelling on the third floor with mechanical air conditioning has a ceiling height of 2.20 m. Is this compliant?' Which answer is correct?

options.text: Non-compliant — a 2.70 m minimum applies to all habitable rooms in all Group A dwellings regardless of floor level or ventilation type
Non-compliant — the third storey minimum for artificially ventilated buildings is 2.40 m, which 2.20 m does not meet
Compliant — the third storey and above minimum for artificially ventilated buildings is 2.10 m; 2.20 m exceeds this threshold
Compliant — mezzanine clearance rules (1.80 m) apply to third-floor rooms with low ceilings in compact dwellings

questions.rationale: Sec. 805 sets a descending scale for artificially ventilated multi-storey buildings: 1st floor = 2.70 m, 2nd floor = 2.40 m, 3rd floor and above = 2.10 m (unobstructed headroom clearance). A third-floor room at 2.20 m exceeds the 2.10 m minimum — compliant. Option A incorrectly applies the 2.70 m natural ventilation standard to all floors. Option B applies the second-floor 2.40 m minimum to the third floor. Option D applies the mezzanine rule incorrectly.

Compliant — mezzanine clearance rules (1.80 m) apply to third-floor rooms with low ceilings in compact dwellings

questions.rationale: Sec. 805 sets a descending scale for artificially ventilated multi-storey buildings: 1st floor = 2.70 m, 2nd floor = 2.40 m, 3rd floor and above = 2.10 m (unobstructed headroom clearance). A third-floor room at 2.20 m exceeds the 2.10 m minimum — compliant. Option A incorrectly applies the 2.70 m natural ventilation standard to all floors. Option B applies the second-floor 2.40 m minimum to the third floor. Option D applies the mezzanine rule incorrectly.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 806(1)(a), which pair of minimum requirements must BOTH be simultaneously satisfied for a room to qualify as a habitable room in a Group A dwelling?

options.text: Minimum 6.00 sq.m. floor area AND minimum 2.00 m least dimension — both conditions independently required
Minimum 6.00 sq.m. floor area only — the least dimension is a recommended guideline, not a mandatory requirement
Minimum 7.00 sq.m. floor area AND minimum 2.40 m least dimension — the Philippine standard aligned with IRC 2021
Minimum 8.00 sq.m. floor area AND minimum 2.00 m least dimension — applying the larger-room standard for tropical climates

questions.rationale: Sec. 806(1)(a) establishes two simultaneous requirements: 6.00 sq.m. minimum floor area AND 2.00 m minimum least dimension. Both must be met — a room passing area but failing dimension (e.g., 4.0 m x 1.5 m = 6.0 sq.m., least dim 1.5 m < 2.00 m) is non-compliant. Option B incorrectly treats the least dimension as optional. Options C and D cite wrong values.

questions.text: A Group A dwelling has a kitchen that measures 2.00 m x 1.50 m (3.00 sq.m.). Does this kitchen comply with PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 806(1)(b)?

options.text: No — the kitchen fails because the minimum kitchen area is 4.50 sq.m. with a least dimension of 1.80 m
Yes — the kitchen meets the minimum 3.00 sq.m. floor area requirement but must be checked further for the 1.50 m least dimension
Yes — the kitchen satisfies both the 3.00 sq.m. minimum area and the 1.50 m minimum least dimension simultaneously
No — the kitchen fails because 1.50 m is below the 2.00 m least dimension required for all habitable rooms including kitchens

questions.rationale: Sec. 806(1)(b) requires kitchens to have a minimum floor area of 3.00 sq.m. with a minimum least dimension of 1.50 m (not 2.00 m — that is the habitable room standard). A 2.00 m x 1.50 m kitchen = 3.00 sq.m. and has a least dimension of exactly 1.50 m. Both criteria are met exactly. Option A cites wrong values. Option D incorrectly applies the habitable room least dimension (2.00 m) to kitchens.

questions.text: A Group A dwelling is naturally ventilated throughout. Per PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 805, what is the minimum ceiling height for the bedroom on the second floor?

options.text: 2.10 m — the minimum for upper floors in multi-storey buildings under Rule VIII, Sec. 805, applicable only to artificially ventilated spaces
2.40 m — the minimum for the second storey under the artificial ventilation provisions, which does not apply to naturally ventilated buildings
2.70 m — the minimum for ALL habitable rooms in naturally ventilated buildings regardless of floor level
1.80 m — the mezzanine clearance which applies to second-floor rooms in compact dwellings, provided the total floor area does not exceed 50 sqm

questions.rationale: Sec. 805 specifies: for buildings with natural ventilation, all habitable rooms require a minimum ceiling height of 2.70 m regardless of floor level. The descending scale (2.70 m → 2.40 m → 2.10 m) only applies to multi-storey buildings with artificial (mechanical) ventilation. A naturally ventilated second-floor bedroom must still comply with the 2.70 m minimum. Options A and B apply the artificial ventilation scale to a naturally ventilated building. Option D applies the mezzanine clearance.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule VII, Sec. 708(a), what are the maximum lot coverage percentages for a Group A single-family dwelling on a corner lot versus an inside lot?

options.text: 80% for corner lots and 70% for inside lots — reflecting the stricter setback requirements on inside lots
90% for corner lots and 80% for inside lots — corner lots have two street frontages allowing more generous coverage
70% for corner lots and 60% for inside lots — the Philippine standard aligning with typical US residential zoning
90% for both lot types — PD 1096 does not distinguish between corner and inside lots for Group A dwellings

Corner lots have frontage on two streets, giving greater access and light, hence the more generous 90% allowance. Option A reverses the values. Option C is not supported by PD 1096. Option D is incorrect — Sec. 708(a) explicitly distinguishes by lot type.

questions.text: The Building Official inspects a Group A dwelling and finds that the combined toilet and bath room measures 1.05 m x 1.10 m. What is the Code compliance finding under PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 806(1)(c)?

options.text: Compliant — 1.05 m x 1.10 m = 1.155 sq.m., which exceeds the 1.00 sq.m. minimum for bath/toilet rooms
Non-compliant — the area (1.155 sq.m.) exceeds 1.20 sq.m. minimum but the 900 mm least dimension is not met
Non-compliant — the area (1.155 sq.m.) is below the 1.20 sq.m. minimum, and the least dimension (1.05 m) is above 900 mm
Non-compliant — both the area (1.155 sq.m. < 1.20 sq.m.) and the dimension (1.05 m > 900 mm) fail the minimum

questions.rationale: Sec. 806(1)(c) requires bath/toilet rooms to have a minimum area of 1.20 sq.m. AND a minimum least dimension of 900 mm. Area: 1.05 x 1.10 = 1.155 sq.m. — this is BELOW the 1.20 sq.m. minimum, so the room fails on area. Least dimension: 1.05 m = 1050 mm — this exceeds the 900 mm minimum, so it passes on dimension. Non-compliant because area test fails. Option A uses a wrong 1.00 sq.m. threshold. Option D incorrectly states the dimension also fails.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 811, what is the minimum natural ventilation window area required for a habitable room with a floor area of 20 sq.m.?

options.text: 0.80 sq.m. — 4% of 20 sq.m., the IBC standard adopted in the Philippine Code
1.00 sq.m. — the absolute minimum regardless of floor area, applied because 10% of 20 sq.m. equals 2.00 sq.m. but the minimum floor governs
2.00 sq.m. — 10% of the 20 sq.m. floor area per Sec. 811, which exceeds the 1.00 sq.m. absolute minimum
1.60 sq.m. — 8% of 20 sq.m., the IRC standard referenced in the Philippine Code

questions.rationale: Sec. 811 requires natural ventilation window area of at least 10% of the room's floor area, with an absolute minimum of 1.00 sq.m. For a 20 sq.m. room: 10% x 20 = 2.00 sq.m. Since 2.00 sq.m. > 1.00 sq.m. absolute minimum, the percentage rule governs — 2.00 sq.m. is required. Option B incorrectly applies the 1.00 sq.m. floor when the percentage calculation exceeds it. Options A and D apply the IBC and IRC standards respectively, not PD 1096.

questions.text: Under PD 1096, Rule VII, Sec. 708(a), a Group A dwelling must be at least 2 meters from the property line. An architect proposes a corner lot development of 8 m x 12 m (96 sq.m.) with maximum lot coverage. What is the actual achievable building footprint considering BOTH the 90% coverage limit and the 2-meter setback requirement?

options.text: 86 sq.m. — 90% of 96 sq.m., applying only the lot coverage percentage
32 sq.m. — (8−4) x (12−4) = 4 m x 8 m = 32 sq.m. after applying 2 m setback on all sides
48 sq.m. — applying a single 2 m setback on only the two street-facing sides of the corner lot
64 sq.m. — (8−2) x (12−2) = 6 m x 10 m = 60 sq.m., applying the setback on only two sides

questions.rationale: The 2-meter setback applies on all sides per Sec. 708(a). On an 8 m x 12 m lot with 2 m setback on all four sides, the buildable area is (8−4) x (12−4) = 4 m x 8 m = 32 sq.m. The 90% coverage maximum would allow 86 sq.m., but the setback constraint (32 sq.m.) is far more restrictive and governs. This illustrates the critical trap: the coverage percentage and setback minimum are independent constraints, and the more restrictive one governs.

questions.text: Under PD 1096, Rule VIII, Sec. 807, what is the minimum air space per person required for habitable rooms in a Group A dwelling, and how much floor area is needed in a room with a 2.70 m ceiling to legally accommodate 2 persons?

options.text: 10.00 cu.m. per person; a room of 7.40 sq.m. with 2.70 m ceiling provides 20.00 cu.m. for 2 persons
14.00 cu.m. per person; a room needs at least 10.37 sq.m. floor area at 2.70 m ceiling height for 2 persons
14.00 cu.m. per person; a room with 2.70 m ceiling needs 6.00 sq.m. minimum for any number of persons
12.00 cu.m. per person; a room needs at least 8.89 sq.m. floor area at 2.70 m ceiling height for 2 persons

questions.rationale: Sec. 807 requires 14.00 cu.m. of air space per person. For 2 persons: 2 x 14.00 = 28.00 cu.m. needed. With a 2.70 m ceiling: floor area = 28.00 ÷ 2.70 = 10.37 sq.m. minimum. Option A uses the wrong 10 cu.m. value. Option C incorrectly states 6.00 sq.m. is sufficient for any number of persons (6.00 sq.m. is only the minimum area, not an occupancy-independent standard). Option D uses the wrong 12 cu.m. value.
